readings.title: Smaller servings and a second helping
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A workplace canteen noticed that much of its cooked rice returned on unfinished plates. The staff initially considered removing rice from two menus. Interviews suggested a simpler explanation: everyone received the same large serving. The canteen introduced a smaller default portion and allowed free second helpings. During the first week, staff explained the change at the counter so diners would not mistake it for a reduction in value. Food left on plates fell, while people with larger appetites could still eat enough. The change addressed different needs without requiring diners to predict their appetite perfectly.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Planning meals from what is already there
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Before shopping, Tomas used to write a menu and buy every ingredient on it. Food already in his cupboard was often forgotten. He began spending ten minutes checking his shelves before choosing meals. A tin of beans or an unopened bag of noodles could become the starting point for dinner. His shopping list became shorter, but he did not try to avoid buying fresh food. He simply connected new purchases with what he already had. After a month, he found fewer forgotten items and spent less time deciding what to cook when he returned from work.

readings.title: The price beside the package
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At a neighbourhood workshop, shoppers compared several packages of the same dry cereal. The largest package looked economical, but its price per kilogram was slightly higher than that of a smaller one on promotion. The instructor asked participants to compare unit prices rather than package size alone. She also reminded them to consider how much they would actually use. A low unit price was not a saving if half the food remained unwanted. Participants practised making a choice using both price and expected use. The workshop treated careful shopping as a matter of comparison, not simply buying more.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A recipe recorded by more than one cook
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community kitchen collected recipes from its members. Some experienced cooks wrote instructions such as 'add enough water' or 'cook until ready'. These worked for them but confused beginners. The group invited a new member to follow each recipe while its author watched. Questions revealed missing details about quantities and signs of readiness. Authors then revised the instructions, sometimes adding photographs of texture rather than exact times. The finished collection preserved personal cooking styles while making the process easier to follow. Explaining familiar actions to someone else helped the experienced cooks notice knowledge they had never written down.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
Reducing waste often begins with noticing what we already have. A short check of the cupboard can change a shopping plan and suggest a meal. This does not require a perfect system or a strict rule against buying anything new. It requires a habit of connecting today's choices with existing supplies. Small decisions repeated regularly can make daily routines both simpler and less wasteful.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 注意what宾语从句、against buying以及both...and并列结构。
translation.referenceAnswer: 减少浪费往往始于留意我们已经拥有的东西。简单查看一下食品柜，就可能改变购物计划，并带来一餐饭的灵感。这并不需要完美的系统，也不需要严格禁止购买任何新东西。它需要的是一种习惯，把今天的选择与现有物资联系起来。经常重复这些小小的决定，可以让日常生活既更简单，也更少浪费。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English for a workplace canteen notice. Propose a way to reduce food left on plates, explain how diners can still get enough food, and invite feedback on the proposal.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 覆盖减少剩食方法、吃饱保障和反馈渠道。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Our canteen is considering a smaller first serving of rice to reduce food left on plates. Diners have different appetites, and the same large portion does not suit everyone.
Under the proposal, anyone who would like more rice can return to the counter for a free second helping. The choice of dishes will remain the same. Staff will explain the arrangement clearly, so nobody needs to worry about leaving lunch hungry.
We suggest trying this system for two weeks. During that time, please tell the canteen team whether the first portion is suitable and whether getting more food is convenient. Comments can be left on the short form beside the exit. Your experience will help us adjust the system and serve meals with less waste.
